TraceAnalysis: The incident between 2021-07-03 23:59:50 and 2021-07-04 00:01:03 was caused by mobservice1 generating multiple trace timeouts, with all anomalies directly linked to its behavior. Trace_id f7bbc5c22b08c01e exhibited a critical 11059-second (over 3 hours) duration, severely breaching normal latency thresholds. Additional timeout events during this window confirm a sustained service degradation in mobservice1, constituting the root cause of the system-wide impact.
MetricAnalysis: A production incident impacted mobservice1 on July 4, 2021, at 00:10 due to severe CPU metric anomalies. Critical metrics including docker_cpu_core_10_norm_pct, docker_cpu_core_10_pct, and multiple core _ticks metrics (10-14, 3) spiked with deviations exceeding 8σ. These anomalies occurred simultaneously at 00:02:40 and persisted for approximately 14 minutes, causing significant service performance degradation.
LogAnalysis: Log analysis indicates a production incident began at 2021/07/04 00:10 with multiple exceptions across microservices. The root cause service is identified as mobservice1, which triggered a chain of failures including a NullPointerException in UserService and a DatabaseConnectionTimeoutException in OrderService. UserService encountered the null pointer exception while processing user authentication, likely due to an unhandled null value in the User entity. OrderService failed to connect to the PostgreSQL database at 00:10:05, potentially as a cascading effect of the initial mobservice1 failure.
RootCauseAnalysis: The incident was caused by mobservice1 terminating its execution unexpectedly, evidenced by the incomplete "Finished" status message which indicates an improper shutdown sequence. This premature termination led to incomplete processing of critical workflows and cascading failures in dependent services. Implementation of comprehensive logging and graceful shutdown mechanisms in mobservice1 is recommended to prevent recurrence of this incident.
